rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the concessions and competing demands, believers should recite as much Quran as is manageable without imposing hardship.
rows.anchor: فاقرأوا ما تيسر من القرآن من غير تحمل المشاق فإن قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions were burdened by keeping to the prescribed measure of night prayer, not by night worship itself; it may also have felt heavy before the concession.
rows.anchor: الثقلة لم تكن في قيامه بل في محافظة القدر الفروض كما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says night worship came easily to many Successors, naming Abu Hanifa, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Fudayl ibn Iyad, Abu Sulayman al-Darani, Malik ibn Dinar, and Ali ibn Bakkar.
rows.anchor: أبو حنيفة وسعيد بن المسيب وفضيل بن عياش وأبو سليمان اداراني ومالك بن دينار وعلي بن بكار

rows.speaker: علي بن بكار الشامي
rows.claim: Ali ibn Bakkar said that for forty years nothing grieved him except the arrival of dawn, which ended his night vigil.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن بكار الشامي منذ أربعين سنة لم يحزني شيء إلا طلوع الفجر

rows.speaker: عثمان وتميم الداري
rows.claim: The author notes that Uthman and Tamim al-Dari each completed the Quran in one rakah.
rows.anchor: ثم كان من ر بعضهم إنه ختم القرآن في ركعة واحدة كعثمان وتميم الداري رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes the zakat here as zakat al-fitr, since Mecca had no other zakat then, and says it became obligatory later.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي زكاة الفطر إذا لم يكن بمكة زكاة غيرها وإنما وجبت بعدها

rows.speaker: من فسرها بالزكاة المفروضة
rows.claim: Those who read this as obligatory zakat regard the sura's final passage as Medinan, treating its ruling as one whose legislation followed its revelation.
rows.anchor: ومن فسرها بالزكاة المفروضة جعل آخر السورة مدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later prescription and payment of zakat signals that God would fulfill His promise to the Messenger, establish His religion, and make it prevail.
rows.anchor: ففيه دلالة على أنه سينجز وعده لرسوله ويقيم دينه ويظهره حتى تفرض الزكاة وتؤدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qard literally denotes cutting; a loan is so called because the money is cut off from its owner's property subject to repayment in kind.
rows.anchor: والقرض ضرب من القطع وسمى ما يدفع إلى الإنسان من المال بشرط رد بدله قرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good loan means voluntary charitable spending, distinct from obligatory duties whose repayment is assured; the command urges supererogatory giving.
rows.anchor: أريد به الانفاقات في سبيل الخيرات غير المفروض فإنها كالفرض الذي لا خلف في أدائه وفيه حث على التطوع

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that wealth carries a due beyond zakat; giving it well means choosing excellent, useful property for the poor with sincere intention.
rows.anchor: وهو إخراجها من أطيب الأموال وأكثرها نفعا للفقراء بحسن النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zakat command requires giving, whereas the loan command additionally qualifies the gift as good; calling charity a loan likens its return to repayment with increase.
rows.anchor: تسمية الإنفاق لوجه الله أقراضا استعارة تشبيها له بالإقراض من يحث إنما أنفقه يعود عليه مع زيادة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the loan as reciting glorification, praise, the testimony of divine unity, and takbir, as well as spending in God's cause, following Umar's explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم هو قول سبحان الله والحمد ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر والنفقة في سبيل الله كما قال عمر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation includes spending on one's household; a hadith says food a Muslim gives himself and his family counts as charity when done with good intention.
rows.anchor: أو النفقة على الأهل وفي الحديث ما أطعم المسلم نفسه وأهل بيته فهو له صدقة أي يؤجر عليه بحسن نيته

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali transmits al-Baqillani's view that claiming complete freedom from self-interest is unbelief, since freedom from motive is a divine prerogative; apparent God-directed action may conceal a motive.
rows.anchor: روى الامام الغزالي رحمه الله عن القاضي الباقلاني إن ادعاء البراءة من الغرض بالكلية كفر لأن التنزه خاصة إلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim about hidden motives concerns people still on the path of spiritual aspiration; those annihilated from will, the most complete, have no motive, a state known only to their peers or through God's disclosure.
rows.anchor: هذا وارد على أهل الإرادة وإما أهل الفناء عن الإرادة وهم أل النهاية الأكملون فلا غرض لهم أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever good a person sends ahead, whether already mentioned or not, will be found with God as a better and greater reward than what is deferred until a deathbed bequest.
rows.anchor: أي خير كان مما ذكر وما لم يذكر

words: تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًۭا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًۭا
rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says the reward found with God is better than worldly enjoyment and greater in recompense, since God rewards believers without reckoning.
rows.anchor: وفي كشف الأسرار تجدوا ثوابه خيرا لكم من متاع الدنيا وأعظم أجرا لأن الله يعطي المؤمن أجره بغير حساب

words: تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًۭا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the main parsing, khayran is the second object of تجدوا after the pronoun object; aʿẓama coordinates with it, and ajran is a specification of the subject relation.
rows.anchor: قوله خيرا ثاني مفعولي تجدوا وهو تأكيد للمفعول الأول لتجدوه وفصل بينه وبين المفعول الثاني

words: تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًۭا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًۭا
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another grammarian takes وجد here as 'to find' rather than 'to know,' hence it governs one object and khayran is circumstantial from the pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم المشهور إن وجد إذا كان بمعنى صادف يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد وهو ههنا بمعناه

words: تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًۭا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr denotes the return or recompense yielded by an action, whether worldly or in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: والأجر ما يعود من ثواب العمل دنيويا كان أو أخرويا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says every person arrives according to what he sent ahead and regrets what he left behind.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث اعلموا إن كل امرىء على ما قدم قادم وعلى ما خلف نادم

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: At death, the person asks what he left behind while the angels point to what he sent ahead.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه اسلام إن العبد إذا مات قال الإنسان ما خلف وقالت الملائكة ما قدم

rows.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Passing al-Baqi cemetery, Umar greeted its dead and said their wives had remarried, homes occupied, and wealth divided; a voice replied that what was sent ahead was found, what was spent profited, and what was left behind was lost.
rows.anchor: ومر عمر رضي الله عنه ببقيع الغرقداى مقبرة المذدينة لأنها كانت منبت الغرقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet exhorts readers to send good ahead before death because there is no route to lasting life.
rows.anchor: قدم لنفسك قبل موتك صالحا واعمل فليس إلى الخلود سبيل

rows.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: When Umar gave a poor man dates mixed with milk, he answered critics that the poor man's Lord knew the value of the gift.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر لكن رب المسكين يدري ما هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet says to cast good into the water: even if the fish does not know, God knows, supporting hidden charitable giving.
rows.anchor: تونيكى كن بآب اندازاى شاه اكر ما هي نداند داند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seek God's forgiveness continually, at every time and in every condition, because people seldom escape negligence or shortcoming.
rows.anchor: سلوا الله المغفرة لذنوبكم في جميع أوقاتكم وكافة أحوالكم فإن الإنسان قلما يخلوه عن تفريط

rows.speaker: السلف الصالح
rows.claim: The righteous early Muslims prayed until dawn, then sat seeking forgiveness until the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: وكان السلف الصالح يصلون إلى طلوع الفجر ثم يجلسون للاستغفار إلى صلاة الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recommends formulas of forgiveness drawn from Quranic divine names, including 'I ask forgiveness of God, for God is Oft-Returning' and 'O Lord, forgive and show mercy.'
rows.anchor: واستحب الاستغفار على الأسماء من القرآن مثل أن يقول استغفر الله إنه كان توابا استغفر الله إن الله غفور رحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafur forgives sins other than associating partners with God, while Rahim turns bad deeds into good deeds.
rows.anchor: يغفر ما دون أن يشرك به

rows.speaker: عين المعاني
rows.claim: Ayn al-Maʻani glosses Ghafur as covering the failings of the ignorant and negligent, and Rahim as easing their burden.
rows.anchor: وفي عين المعاني غفور يستر على أهل الجهل والتقصير رحيم يخفف عن أهل الجهل والتوفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing that God's forgiveness is not daunted by any sin should make a person ask forgiveness more often; the request is sound with humility, complete with repentance, and empty without either.
rows.anchor: ثم إن كان مع الانكسار فهو صحيح وإن كان مع التوبة فهو كامل وإن كان عريا عنهما فهو باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says writing the master formula of forgiveness and giving it to someone struggling to die will loosen the person's tongue and ease death, a remedy he says has been tried repeatedly.
rows.anchor: ومن كتب سيد الاستغفار وجرعه لمن صعب عليه الموت انطلق لسانه وسهل عليه الموت وقد جرب مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives the master formula: acknowledge God as Lord and creator, affirm servitude and covenant, seek refuge from one's deeds, confess favors and sin, and ask forgiveness from God alone.
rows.anchor: اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Single out the Lord for takbir: affirm His majesty in belief and speech and exalt Him above the descriptions of idolaters and other wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وخصص ربك بالتكبير وهو صوفه تعالى بالكبرياء اعتقادا وقولا وعظمة عما يقول فيه عبدة الأثوان

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام وخديجة
rows.claim: A report says that on revelation the Prophet declared God great, Khadija followed, rejoiced, and recognized it as revelation because Satan would not command takbir.
rows.anchor: ويروى إنه لما نزل قال رسول الله عليه السلام الله أكبر فكبرت خديجة أيضا وفرحت وأيقنت إنه الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's postures and forms imply limitation, so takbir belongs within prayer to declare God free of every determination, even though prayer was not yet established at the start of prophethood.
rows.anchor: ودخل فيه تبكير الصلاة وإن لم يكن في أوائل لنبوة صلاة وذلك لأن الصلاة عبارة عن أوضاع وهيئات كلها تعطي التقييد

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A sound report says God's face is in correspondence with the servant's face during prayer.
rows.anchor: فلزم التكبير فيها لأن وجه الله يحاذى وجه العبد حينئذ على ما ورد في الخبر الصيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the fa as conditional: whatever happens, do not stop magnifying and describing God as supreme.
rows.anchor: والفاء لمعنى الشرط كأنه قيل ما كان أي أي شيء حدث فلا تدع تكبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fa sequences the first aim of the command to rise: glorify God, since knowing the Creator comes before declaring Him beyond what is unworthy of Him.
rows.anchor: أو للدلالة على أن المقصود الأول من الأمر بالقيام أن يبكر رب وينزهه عن الشكر فإن أول ما يجب معرفة الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's majesty is intrinsic and self-subsisting, not dependent on those who magnify Him; no created act can encompass His greatness.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن كبرياءه تعالى ذاتي له قائمبنفسه لا بغيره من المكبرين فهو أكبر من أن يكبره غيره

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: At the Mi'raj the Prophet said he could not encompass God's praise, for God is as He praised Himself.
rows.anchor: ولذا قال عليه السلام ليلة المعراج لا أحصى ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward command is to wash garments with pure water, preserve them from impurity, and avoid carrying filth both in prayer and outside it.
rows.anchor: فطهرها مما ليس بطاهر بحفظها وصيانتها عن النجاسات وغسلها بالماء الطاهر بعد تلطخها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purifying garments can also mean shortening them so they do not drag through dirt; the preferred length is mid-shin or the ankle, and the Prophet warned against what falls below the ankle.
rows.anchor: وبتقصيرها أيضا فإن طولها يؤدي إلى جر الذيول على القاذورات فيكون التطهير كناية عن التقصير

rows.speaker: علي المرتضى رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali al-Murtada is quoted in Persian as advising that garments be kept short.
rows.anchor: وحضرت مرتضى رضي الله عنه كفت كوتاه كن جامه را

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was the first command to abandon blameworthy customs: polytheists did not keep their garments clear of impurity, while inner purification should lead to outward cleanliness.
rows.anchor: وهو أول ما أمر به عليه السلام من رفض العادت المذمومة فإن المشركين ما كانوا يصونون ثيابهم عن النجاسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command moves from cleansing the inward self to the outward garment; whoever purifies the heart naturally avoids filth and chooses purity in all things.
rows.anchor: فه انتقال من تطهير الباطن إلى تطهير الظاهر لأن الغالب إن من نقى باطنه أبي إلا اجتناب الخبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites sayings that religion rests on cleanliness, only the clean enter Paradise, and God loves the clean worshipper.
rows.anchor: فإن الدين بنى على النظافة ولا يدخل الجنة إلا نظيف والله يحب الناسك النظيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says washing a vessel and cleaning a courtyard bring wealth.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث غسل الإناء وطهارة الفناء يورثن الغنى

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A marfu report urges cleaning the mouth because it is a path through which Quran is recited.
rows.anchor: وفي المرفوع نظفوا أفواهكم فإنها طرق القرآن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes bodily from spiritual purification; the verse may address both, and is also read as commanding the self to be cleansed of defects.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الطهارة ضربان طهارة جسم وطهارة نفس وقد حمل عليهما عامة الآيات

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses rahq as being overtaken and engulfed by force; the verb can be transitive in the sense of making someone bear a burden.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : رهقه الأمر غشيه بقهر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Suud is a difficult ascent or steep hill, and by extension any hardship; grammatically it is the second object of ارهق.
rows.anchor: والصعود العقبة الشاقة ويستعار لكل مشاق وهو مفعول ثان لأرحق

rows.speaker: بعض التفاسير
rows.claim: Some commentaries parse suud as a verbal noun in the active sense, like a steep hill, or as a passive participle from climbing; its masculine form may follow an implied road or the pattern of kawud.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير صعودا إما فعول بمعنى فاعل يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث مثل عقبة كؤود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of the increase he covets, God will force him up a steep, difficult path whose intense hardship surrounds him on every side.
rows.anchor: والمعنى سأكلفه كرها بدل ما يطمعه من الزيادة ارتقاء عقبه شاقة المصعد

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali interprets the ascent as a condition in which the soul climbs during death throes, even if death does not immediately follow.
rows.anchor: وقال الغزالي رحمه الله حالة تصعد فيها نفسه للنزع وإن لم يتعقبه موت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascent can symbolize unbearable punishment or be taken literally as a mountain of fire climbed repeatedly.
rows.anchor: وهو مثال لما يلقى من العذاب الصعب الذي لا يطاق ويجوز أن يحمل على حقيقته

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to describe Suud as a mountain of fire climbed for seventy years before the climber falls, endlessly.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام الصعود جبل من نار يصعد فيه سبعين خريفا ثم يهوى كذا أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharif here means a year: autumn closes the year as its fruit is completed and harvested.
rows.anchor: قوله سبعين خريفا أي سبعين عاما لأن الخريف آخر السنة فيه تتم الثمار وتدرك

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A further Prophetic report says hands and feet melt on the fiery ascent and return when lifted, while he is driven onward with blows until reaching the summit.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام يكلف أن يصعد عقبه في لنار كلما وضع يده عليها ذابت فإذا رفعها عادت

rows.speaker: تاج المصادر
rows.claim: The cited lexicon glosses tafkir as thinking or reflecting.
rows.anchor: بمعنى التفكر والتأمل كما قال في تاج المصادر التفكير انديشه كردن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqdir means measuring, arranging, and preparing; the man considered what to say to attack the Quran and rehearsed it within himself.
rows.anchor: والتقدير اندازه وتهيئه كردن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase marvels at his calculation as if it hit the Quraysh's target, though calling the Quran magic is a feeble and absurd conclusion.
rows.anchor: تعجيب من تقديره وإصابته فيه الغرض الذي كان ينتحيه قريش قاتلهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase mocks Quraysh for quoting the curse and admiring their own estimate; 'May God kill him' can express astonishment at extreme skill in poetry or bravery.
rows.anchor: أو حكاية لما ذكروه من قولهم قتل كيف قدر تهكما بهم وبإعجابهم بتقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He points back to his fuller explanation of the idiom 'May God fight them' in the sura al-Munafiqun.
rows.anchor: وقد سبق في قاتلهم الله في المنافقين مزيد البيان

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Walid heard the Prophet reciting al-Sajda, or according to some commentaries the opening of Ha Mim al-Mumin, and told Banu Makhzum the speech was neither human nor jinn.
rows.anchor: إن الوليد مر بالنبي عليه السلام وهو يقر أحم السجدة وفي بعض التفاسير فواتح سورة حم المؤمن

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Walid praised the Quran's sweetness and beauty, saying its top bore fruit and its bottom flowed abundantly, like a fresh, well-rooted tree.
rows.anchor: والله لقد سمعت من محمد آنفا كلاما ما هو من كلام الأنس ولا من كلام الجن إن له لحلاوة وإن عليه لطلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is likened to a verdant tree with a strong root, fruitful upper branches, and a richly watered lower part.
rows.anchor: شبه القرآن بالشجرة الغضة الطرية التي استحكم أصلها بكثرة الماء وأثمرت فروعها في السماء

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi's Persian rendering describes the Quran as uniquely sweet and fresh, with fruits of complete felicity above and roots of virtues and wisdom below.
rows.anchor: مراورا حلاوتي وعذوبتي هست كه هي سخن رانباشد وبروى طر أوتى وتازكي هست كه هي حديثي رانبود

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: When Walid said the Quran triumphs and cannot be surpassed, Quraysh accused him of apostasy; Abu Jahl offered to deal with him and approached him while he sat grieving.
rows.anchor: ثم قال الوليد وإنه يعلو ولا يعلى فقالت قريش صبأ والله الوليد أي مال عن دينه

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl accused Walid of praising Muhammad to curry favor for food scraps; Walid answered that Quraysh had wealth and Muhammad's followers were too poor to feed anyone.
rows.anchor: توسخنان محمدا عليه السلام سند ميدهى وآنرا بزرك ميدارى وثنا ميكويى تا از فضله طعام ايشان بهره بردارى

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Walid told Quraysh that Muhammad's reputation had spread among Arabs and the pilgrimage season was near, so they needed to agree what answer to give visitors.
rows.anchor: بدانيدكه حال وكار اين محمد در عرب منتشر كشت وموسم حج نزديكست كه عرب مى آيند وازحال وى رسند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the four vices may have jointly brought each person to the Fire, or different people may have entered for different vices; either reading shows their persistence in Saqar resulted from these faults.
rows.anchor: يحتمل الأمرين جميعا كافي الكشاف وفيه إشارة إلى أن بقاءهم في سقر الظبيعة إنما كان بسبب هذه الرذائل والذمائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if intercessors hypothetically assembled to plead for them, their pleading would not help: intercession requires divine permission and a receptive recipient, which an unbeliever is not.
rows.anchor: أي لو قدر اجتماعهم على شفاعتهم على سبيل فرض المحال لا تنفعهم تلك الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction proves that intercession itself is real and will benefit sinful believers; otherwise specifying that unbelievers gain no benefit would be pointless.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على صحة الشفاعة ونفعنا يومئذ لعصاة المؤمنين وإلا لما كان لتخصيصهم بعدم منفعة الشفاعة وجه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says angels, prophets, martyrs, the righteous, and all believers intercede, leaving only four in the Fire, then cites the offenders' confession in verses 43–46.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه تشفع الملائكة والنبيون والشهداء والصالحون وجميع المؤمنين فلا يبقى في النار إلا أربعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet intercedes three times, followed by angels, prophets, parents, and children, after which God declares that His mercy remains and only the heaven-forbidden remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إن محمدا عليه السلام يشفع ثلاث مرات ثم تشفع الملائكة ثم الأنبياء ثم الآباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author relates that people in Hell remind people in Paradise of favors such as giving drink, ablution water, food, or clothing; the latter intercede and they enter Paradise, before or after Hell.
rows.anchor: أنا الذي سقيتك شربة ويقول آخر أنا الذي وهبت لك وضوأ ويقول آخر أطعمتك لقمة وآخر كسوتك خرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question follows the dreadful fate of the deniers: with so many reasons to accept and take heed from the Quran, what could make them turn away without cause?
rows.anchor: الفاء لترتيب أنكال إعراضهم عن القرآن بغير سبب على ما قبلها من موجبت الإقبال عليه والاتعاظ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma is interrogative, mu'ridin is a circumstantial accusative for the pronoun in the locative predicate, and ʿan is attached to it.
rows.anchor: ومعرضين حال من الضمير في الجار الوقع خبرا لما الاستفهامسية وعن متعلقة به

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar glosses the turning away as either denial or refusal to follow the reminder.
rows.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" س ه رشسيدست ايشانراكه ازنين ندى روكردانيده انده يقال لإعراض يكون بالجحود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey comparison is another circumstantial clause, linked by overlap to the implied subject of mu'ridin; humur is the plural of donkey and can denote wild asses here.
rows.anchor: حال من المستكن في معرضين بطريق التداخل وحمر جمع حمار وهو معروف ويكون وحشيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istanfara can mean that an animal fled, like nafara; al-Zamakhshari alternatively keeps the sense of seeking flight, as if the asses drove themselves into flight.
rows.anchor: فاستنفر بمعنى نفر كما إن استعجب بمعنى عجب وقال الزمخشري كأنهم حمر تطلب النفار من نفوسها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib records kasra on the fa for 'fleeing' and fatha for 'frightened off.'
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : مستنفرة قد قرىء بفتح الفاء وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswara means a lion, which wild asses flee intensely; haydara resembles it in form and sense, and qaswara derives from overpowering and subduing.
rows.anchor: أي من أسد لأن الوحشية إذا عاينت الأسد تهرب أشد الهرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaswara is the Abyssinian word for lion; another view takes it as a band of hunters or archers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : القسورة هو الأسد بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi's Persian gloss lists lions, hunters, ropes or traps, archers, and various noises as things from which they flee.
rows.anchor: (وقال الكاشفي) : كريخنذ از شيريا از صياد ياريسمان دام يا مردم تيرانداز يا آوازهاى مختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rejection and flight from Quranic admonition resemble wild asses driven into frantic flight by what frightens them.
rows.anchor: شبهوا في أعراضهم عن القرآن واستماع ما فيه من المواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian gloss says they flee from listening because they lack a listening ear and an awakened heart; Mathnawi verses likewise contrast them with the living message and its spiritual secret.
rows.anchor: كما أشار إليه في المثنوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey simile is a severe humiliation: wild asses flee exceptionally hard, and calling someone a donkey is an especially harsh insult.
rows.anchor: وفيه من ذمهم وتهجين حالهم ما لا يخفى يعني إن في تشبيههم بالحمر شهادة عليهم بالبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He relates a preacher's joke to a man who lost his donkey: when a listener rose to leave, the preacher told the man to take that listener as his donkey.
rows.anchor: كان يعظ الناس في مسجد جامع وحوله جماعة كثيرة فرأى ذلك رجل من البله وكان قد فقد حماره

words: بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفًۭا مُّنَشَّرَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of accepting the reminder, they stubbornly demand separate heavenly books for every person; Abu Jahl, Abdullah ibn Umayya, and their companions made this demand of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام كأنه قيل لا يكلفون بتلك التذكرة

words: بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفًۭا مُّنَشَّرَةًۭ
rows.speaker: أبو جهل وعبد الله بن أمية وأصحابهما
rows.claim: They demanded a separate page from the Lord of the worlds addressed to each person and ordering him to follow Muhammad; they also said they would not believe without a book to read.
rows.anchor: عنوانها من رب العالمين إلى فلان ابن فلا تؤمر فيها باتباعك أي بأن يقال اتبع محمدا فإنه رسول من قبلي إليك

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines marʾ as a human being or man and gives three forms of its initial hamza and case behavior; it has no plural from the same lexical form.
rows.anchor: في "القاموس" المرء مثلثة الميم الإنسان أو الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the clause, an-na with its complement is the first object of yuridu, the pronoun in yu'ta is the first object of that verb, and suhuf is its second object; munashshara describes suhuf.
rows.anchor: وأن مع صلته مفعول يريد وصحفا مفعول ثان ليؤتى والأول ضمير كل ومنتشرة صفة صحف

rows.speaker: تاج المصادر
rows.claim: Taj al-Masadir says the doubled form munashshara marks abundance or multiplicity.
rows.anchor: قال في تاج المصادر وصحف منتشرة شدد للكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first kalla rebukes their obstinate demand for signs, which seeks defiance rather than guidance; their real cause is lack of fear of the Hereafter, being consumed by love of this world.
rows.anchor: ردع عن اقتراحهم الآيات وإرادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rejection stems from not fearing the next life, not from the failure to receive individual heavenly pages.
rows.anchor: فلعدم خوفهم منها أعرضوا عن التذكرة لا لامتناع إيتاء الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second kalla is a rebuke for turning away from the reminder.
rows.anchor: ردع عن إعراضهم عن التذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in innahu and dhikrihi refers to tadhkira, synonymous with remembrance, or to the Quran, just as mawʿiza can mean admonition and sayha can mean sound.
rows.anchor: الضمير في إنه وفى ذكره للتذكرة لأنها بمعنى الذكر أو القرآن كالموعظة بمعنى الوعظ والصيحة بمعنى الصوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite tadhkira magnifies it as a powerful, sufficient reminder; al-Burhan says it reminds people of truth and that the word was chosen for the rhyme ending.
rows.anchor: أي تذكرة فالتنوين للتعظيم أي تذكرة بليغة كافية وفي برهان القرآن أي تذكير للحق وعدل إليها للفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever chooses may keep the reminder before his eyes and take heed before reaching the grave, thereby gaining happiness in both worlds.
rows.anchor: أن يذكره ويتعظ به قبل الحلول في القبر

words: وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the apparent wording of 'whoever wills may remember,' human willing alone does not determine action; people remember only when God wills it.
rows.anchor: إذ لا تأثير لمشيئته العبد وإرادته في أفعاله وضمير الجمع إما أن يعود إلى الكفرة

words: وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun may refer to the disbelievers in context or, in a general reading, to all accountable people.
rows.anchor: إلى من نظر إلى عموم المعنى لشموله لكل من المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is elliptical from the broadest causes or states: they remember only by God's willing their remembrance, or while He wills it.
rows.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من أعمل العلل أو من أعم الأحوال أي وما يذكرون لعلة من العلل أو في حال من الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone merits being feared, believed, and obeyed, and He is worthy to forgive those who believe in and obey Him.
rows.anchor: حقيق بأن يغفر لمن آمن به وأطعه قال بعضهم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun taqwa is parsed as a verbal noun on a passive pattern.
rows.anchor: فلتقوى مصدر من المبنى للمفعول

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A Sufi gloss defines taqwa as disavowing everything apart from God; keeping proper spiritual manners in taqwa makes one worthy of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم التقوى هو التبري من كل شيء سوى الله فمن لزم الآداب في التقوى فهو أهل المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ʿizam can also derive from ʿazim, great, as in other plural forms such as kiram and kibar.
rows.anchor: ويجيء جمع عظيم أيضا ككرام وكريم وكبار وكبير ومنه الموالي العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier wrongly assumes God cannot gather his decayed bones; God will reassemble them after scattering, dispersal by wind, and loss in land and sea to requite their deeds.
rows.anchor: فإنا نجمعها بعد تشتتها ورجوعها رميما ورقاتا مختلطا بالتراب وبعد ما نسفتها الرياح وطيرتها في أقطار الأرض

rows.speaker: عدي بن ربيعة
rows.claim: A report says Adi ibn Rabi'a, related by marriage to al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, asked Muhammad about the Resurrection and rejected the prospect after hearing his answer, voicing the denier's challenge about reviving decayed bones.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن عدى بن أبي ربيعة ختن الأخنس بن شريف وهما اللذان كان عليه السلام يقول فيهما اللهم اكفني جاري اسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection is phrased like the denier's question in Ya Sin: who can revive bones when they are rotten?
rows.anchor: فيكون الكلام خارجا على قول المنكر كقوله من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation uses bones for the whole person, since bones form the body's frame and its shape stands only when they are properly assembled.
rows.anchor: وقيل ذكر العظام وارد نفسه كلها لأن العظام قالب النفس لا يستوي الخلق إلا باستوائها

words: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some deny resurrection from doubt, but God's ability to revive is certain to a reflective reasoner; the affirmative bala answers the denial by affirming that He will gather them.
rows.anchor: ودل هذا الإنكار على إنه ناشىء من الشبهة وذلك بالنسبة إلى البعض والله قار على الإحياء لا شبهة في بالنسبة إلى القال المتفكر المستدل

words: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadirin is a circumstantial accusative affirming the implied subject of the estimated verb 'We gather them' after bala.
rows.anchor: فهو حال مؤكدة من الضمير المستكن في تجمع المقدر بعد بلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can collect and restore even the tiny phalanges of fingers, so restoring the larger bones is easier still.
rows.anchor: أي نجمع سلامياته ونضم بعضها إلى بعض كما كانت مع صغرها ولطافتها فكيف بكبار العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salami is a plural for the small bones of the hand and foot, on the pattern of habara.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع سلامي كحبارى وهي العظام الصغار ي اليد والرجل

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A hadith says every joint of a person owes charity each day the sun rises, in any form of speech, action, or wealth.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث كلا سلامي من الناس عليه صدقة كل يوم تطلع فيه الشمس أي على صاحبه صدقة من أي أنواع الصدقة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines banan as the fingers or their tips.
rows.anchor: في "القاموس" البنان الأصابع أو أطرافها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says banan is named for the fingertips because they let a person put affairs in order and accomplish what he wants; the verse singles it out for that practical function.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب البنان الأصابع قيل سميت بذلك لأن بها إصلاح الأحوال

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib also cites the command to strike every fingertip to illustrate that the fingers are used to fight and defend.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب البنان الأصابع قيل سميت بذلك لأن بها إصلاح الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banan may also be the fingertips, the last and smallest parts to be formed; it is singular in form but collective in meaning, like tamr, and connotes both smallness and extremity.
rows.anchor: أو المعنى على نسوى أصابعه التي هي أطرافه وآخر ما يتم به خلفه فالبنان مفرد اللفظ مجموع المعنى كالتمر
